data.standardized_narrative: Gross prior-year development at 31 December 2020 shows a small favourable movement (release) of approximately $2.17m on older underwriting years (driven by development on the 2018 underwriting year). This favourable gross development was offset at the net level by large movements in reinsurance recoverables, producing a reported net deterioration of $5.407m within calendar year claims incurred. The reserve movements and overall result were driven by natural catastrophe activity (notably US hurricane and wildfire events) and by the interaction with the reinsurance programme and recoveries.
raw_causal_phrases: Included within net calendar year claims incurred of $46,283,000 is a deterioration of $5,407,000 in claims reserves established at the prior year end.
These natural catastrophe events have contributed to a significant calendar year loss for the syndicate.
As the losses on each event were within the retention of the reinsurance programme, reinsurance recoveries are significantly lower than expectations for the 2020 year of account.

We are disappointed with the 2018 closed year result. The net loss position for the syndicate for 2018 was a consequence of the frequency of catastrophes, particularly in the last quarter of the year, rather than the severity of any individual event.
data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior year development was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative incurred rows). The report also states a net deterioration of $5.407m (net of reinsurance) in prior year reserves; the gross movement is a $2.172m release (derived from the triangle) while reinsurers' share movements were large and caused the net deterioration. Figures are in the syndicate's functional currency (USD). Some named events are referenced but monetary impacts by event are not quantified in the report.
